derivedGrowth20192025.notesOnCausesOfGrowth: Just Value nearly doubled (+88.75%) — well above Clay County's population growth over the same period. The dominant documented driver of Clay County's ad valorem tax growth is RISING PROPERTY VALUES (reassessment plus new construction, not separated in this dataset), not the county raising millage — the Countywide Operating Millage only moved from about 5.24 (2019) to 5.5471 (since FY2023-24), a modest ~5.9% rate increase, versus an 87% dollar increase in the tax actually levied. A true new-construction-vs-reassessment split requires DOR's separate New Construction (DR-403) series, not yet pulled — flagged as still needed.

nonAdValoremAnomaly.label: DATA ANOMALY — NEEDS VERIFICATION

fieldVerification.dorFieldLabel: "Total Non-Ad Valorem Taxes", printed under the "Property Taxes Levied" panel heading on the Clay County page of each vintage year's DOR County Profile PDF
fieldVerification.units: Whole U.S. dollars, whole-county aggregate (not per-parcel, not a rate)
fieldVerification.measureType: This is a LEVY figure (the panel's own heading is "Property Taxes Levied"), not a collections, roll-value, or assessment-roll figure. It should never be described as taxes actually collected or paid by residents.
fieldVerification.sameFieldNameNote: The exact same field label ("Total Non-Ad Valorem Taxes") appears in an identically structured panel in every vintage-year PDF checked (2021 through 2025), suggesting the metric definition itself is stable across years. Whether the underlying UNIVERSE of assessments DOR rolls into that field changed year to year (e.g., a newly created MSBU, a reclassified assessment, a reporting-methodology change at DOR, or an actual new county-level assessment) was not established in this research pass.
fieldVerification.oddityFound: The 2021 and 2022 figures are IDENTICAL to the dollar ($48,876,049), despite Total Taxes and every ad valorem line changing between those two years. This is itself worth independent verification — it may indicate DOR did not re-survey this specific field for the 2022 vintage (a data-staleness/carry-forward artifact) rather than non-ad-valorem assessments genuinely holding flat. If that carry-forward pattern also affected the 2024 or 2025 figure, the apparent 2024-to-2025 jump could be a reporting artifact rather than a real one-year change — this has NOT been ruled out.

whatIsNotEstablished: Whether Clay County's own non-ad-valorem assessment roll shows the same $110M year-over-year change, or a different figure

Whether the change reflects a new/expanded assessment (e.g. stormwater, solid waste, fire, an MSBU), a DOR reporting-methodology change, or a data anomaly/carry-forward artifact like the one observed between 2021 and 2022
Whether the same set of taxing authorities and assessment types is represented in the 2024 and 2025 figures
nonAdValoremAnomaly.doNotPresentAs: An increase in taxes actually paid or collected by Clay County residents; evidence of unexplained county spending; or a $110M new-tax event. None of these are established by the source data reviewed.
nonAdValoremAnomaly.recommendedNextStep: Clay County's own non-ad-valorem assessment roll, or the Tax Collector's combined tax-bill file, compared against DOR's underlying non-ad-valorem worksheet (not just the summary panel) for both years.

statewideContext.accessBlockerNote: Florida DOR's statewide aggregate 'Ad Valorem Valuation and Tax Data Book' is served through a JS-rendered document-library page; individual per-county 'County Profile' PDFs ARE static and directly linkable (floridarevenue.com/property/Documents/{YEAR}_County_Profiles.pdf) and were the primary source for every Clay County figure in this file. A follow-up with browser-based access, or a direct request to PTOResearchAnalysis@floridarevenue.com, would resolve the remaining statewide dollar totals.

explanatoryComponentsForClayCountyRevenu.note: Per the project's standing rule against assuming levy growth minus population minus inflation equals unexplained spending, here is what this dataset supports as explanatory factors for Clay County's 2019-2025 ad valorem growth specifically:
supportedByEvidence: Rising property values (just value +88.75%, county taxable value +76.73%, 2019-2025) — the dominant documented driver of the dollar increase in county ad valorem taxes.
A modest millage increase (5.24 to 5.5471 mills, flat since FY2023-24) — real but small next to the value growth.
A large, not-yet-attributed increase in non-ad-valorem assessments in the most recent year observed (2024-2025, +$110M) — flagged above as unresolved.
notYetInvestigated: New-construction value specifically (DOR publishes this as a separate line item; not pulled this session).
Exemption totals over time beyond the single-year figures captured above.
Voter-approved levies or new MSTU/MSBU districts created 2019-2025.
Commercial vs. residential development mix shift (DOR profiles show a 'Real Property Just Value by Property Type' breakdown per year; visible in raw extracts but not tabulated here).
